title: Blessed Diana Andalò and Blessed Cecilia, Virgins
short_summary: Blessed Diana Andalò and Blessed Cecilia are honored in the Dominican calendar as early women of the Order whose consecrated life helped root Dominican holiness in prayer, community, and fidelity to Christ.
key_facts: The Dominican Calendarium keeps Blessed Diana and Blessed Cecilia as an optional memorial on June 8.
The liturgical color is white when the memorial is celebrated.
The Order of Preachers lists them among the saints and blesseds observed by the Order throughout the world.
Diana Andalò was born in Bologna near the beginning of the thirteenth century.
Their remembrance belongs to the Dominican proper calendar and does not replace the general U.S. calendar day.

sections.heading: Early Dominican women
sections.body: Diana and Cecilia stand near the early growth of Dominican life among women. Their memorial points to a form of holiness marked by consecrated life, prayer, and the shared mission of the Order.

sections.heading: A proper Dominican memorial
sections.body: The app presents this observance only for users who choose the Dominican calendar preference. It remains a local or proper observance, not a universal feast.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Hidden fidelity
catholic_connection_sections.body: Their witness reminds the Church that preaching is sustained by contemplative fidelity and by communities ordered toward Christ.
